items.title: The MOSS campaign closes with a full measurement run, its scorecard, and the README written from it

steps.title: The full measurement run measures every model's scorecard row at the campaign's last commit, MOSS's image rows among them, and the README's tables are written from it
steps.verify: go run ./cmd/validate -scorecard | grep -oE '^\| (Krea-2-Turbo|SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Infographic-V3|SimpleDiffusion-TensorProductAttentionRope|Un-0|MOSS-Image-SFT-797fa8e678b4f) \| image-gen \| [0-9]' | sort -u | wc -l | grep -qx 5 && go run ./cmd/validate -readme && grep -qE '^\| MOSS-Image-SFT-797fa8e678b4f \| [0-9]' README.md
steps.rationale: The owner's order of 2026-11-24: the MOSS rows first, then the campaign's closing measurement, scorecard and README, as the last campaign closed (full-measurement/run, whose check 5147c611f made one pipeline the gate runs). The MOSS rows are landed but served-parts/clock, which times the workflow on the new ledger. The work: a full measurement run of the cycle (validate -run), started outside the session as the last was, at the commit after served-parts/clock, measuring every model's scorecard row with MOSS's sections served as the campaign left them; then the README's tables written from the scorecard (validate -readme). Check: the scorecard holds a measured image-gen row for each of the five image models, MOSS-Image-SFT among them, and the README written from it holds MOSS's row. The check's form is the one the gate took for full-measurement/run, a pipeline with no shell assignment (SQA-483).

items.title: Flash-Next's long-context acceptance has a cause for its failure at 16:44: what its server needs against what the machine had free

steps.title: TestFlashNextLongContextAcceptance runs on a quiet machine, its server's peak recorded against the 71.4 GiB its tree was bound to
steps.rationale: The owner's review of 2026-11-24 (fifth), point 2, checked against lanes.log: valid. The lanes at 5f5d4db92 did not pass: TestFlashNextLongContextAcceptance failed in the models lane at 16:44 after 9 s, its model swap's child server ending before it was ready because the process tree reached its memory limit of 71.4 GiB, the machine's free commit at its start (processcontrol's job bound), and no step named a cause since. Whether the server needs more than the machine holds at Flash-Next's long context, or other work held the memory then, is unmeasured. The step: run the test on a quiet machine (no landing, no lanes), read its server tree's peak commit, and cure what it shows: a context the model's host commit cannot hold is bound by what the machine has, or the test waits for the memory it needs, as the card's turn waits. Check: the test passes on the quiet machine.

items.title: A check's pass is kept while what it read is unchanged, its inputs observed, so a commit runs only the checks its change can alter

steps.title: The gate and the lanes keep a package's pass while its test binary and every file it read are unchanged by content
steps.rationale:
Follows observed-inputs/measure. The change: one rule for every test the gate's stages and the lanes run. A package's pass is kept, by its test binary's identity and the digests of what it read, and a later run whose binary and inputs match takes the kept pass in place of running; any input that differs runs it. Declared inputs and -count=1 go. Check: TestAPassIsKeptWhileWhatItReadIsUnchanged runs a fixture package twice and finds the second taken from the kept pass, then changes the file it reads and finds it run. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

Note: The cause, measured by observed-inputs/measure: go test keeps no pass of a package whose tests start a child process with its stdio unset. os/exec opens the null device for it, the test log records the relative path NUL, go test resolves it inside the package, Windows reports it modified in 2185, and cmd/go refuses an input modified under 2 s ago (errFileTooNew). All 11 host packages surveyed do so. The temporary paths a run reads lie outside the module, which go test never rechecks. So the kept pass this step keeps, keyed by the test binary and the content of what it read, takes NUL for the device it is, not a file, and leaves out what lies outside the repository's module, as go test does. Without that, no package the gate runs would be kept.

Note: Corrected 2026-11-25 at b9bac4955, checked against observed-inputs/measure's readings and cmd/go.

The earlier note's last clause is wrong for the lanes. They run -count=1 because their models and references lie outside the module, which go test never rechecks (SQA-315), so a kept pass must key outside-module inputs too. Only the null device and the test's own temporary files are left out.

The rule as filed is not sound for the gate's packages. A kept pass keyed by what the test binary read cannot see what its child processes read, and every package measured starts children: all 11 surveyed open NUL. Some of those children read the repository itself: commanddoc's builds of each command, go list, git in the trunk. A change those children alone read would pass the gate on a pass kept from before it. go test's cache has the same blind spot, but it never kept a pass here (the null device), so the blind spot never mattered. A rule that can pass a change unchecked costs more than a slow commit.

Before the rule is built, the children's reads must be seen or bounded:
- A child started in a temporary directory, a fixture's repository, reads only what the test made there. One started in the repository reads inputs its parent's log cannot name.
- The rule may keep a pass only of a package whose tests start no child in the repository. That needs the tests' children to start through one helper, which records each child's working directory beside the test log, with a rule holding the tests' raw starts to it.
- Otherwise the step stays unbuilt.

The row is moved after the tooling rows whose steps are sound as filed, until that design is settled and measured: how many packages start a child in the repository.

steps.title: The mechanisms the kept passes make redundant go: the yield to a newer commit, the lanes' rotation and the per-package turn handover
steps.rationale:
Follows observed-inputs/rule. With passes kept by what they read, a run at an older commit spends nothing a newer one repeats, so the run's yield to a newer commit due (plan.Yields, cmd/validate/run.go:276) goes; the lanes need no rotation to reach packages long without a pass (lanes-rotation, which this step retires unworked); and the per-package handover of the test turn (testSteps, landing.HoldTestTurnEach) stays only where a package's own run outlasts a commit's patience, which turn-priority covers. Check: TestNoLaneYieldsOrRotatesWhatAKeptPassCovers finds no yield and no rotation in a lanes run whose packages' passes are kept. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

Note: The lanes' rotation this step removes is lanes-order/do's order, a close's lanes least recently run first (cmd/validate leastRecentlyRunFirst), filed 2026-11-24 for the interval before this step lands. It goes with the yield, once no run spends what a newer one repeats.

items.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test

steps.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test
steps.rationale:
The evidence: cuda-synthetic/tag moved every untagged CUDA test that reads the data root behind modeltest but one. TestSenseNovaVariableRequestResources runs SenseNova's 8B production generation in an isolated measurement process, and docs/image_video_capacity.json names its retained measurement by the bytes of its file (evidence:sha256:888854b5...), which the store holds; tagged, its bytes changed and TestImageVideoCapacityAcceptance found no evidence under the new identity. A measurement is taken again only on a card to itself, and the readings campaign holds the card until its Wan arms are drawn, so the file stays in the gate, named by the check as measuredInPlace, and this row follows the campaign.

The change: the test carries //go:build modeltest, it is measured again on a quiet card into the store, the capacity record and its protocol digest (imageVideoCapacitySHA256) name the new identity, and measuredInPlace goes, so internal/sensenovarecipe leaves the cuda lane.

Check: a whole-tree test with measuredInPlace gone, named afresh so it fails before the change: TestTheGateRunsNoRealModelTest.

Refiled 2026-11-16 from cuda-resources/do, whose step carried no card need, so dispatch gave it while the readings campaign held the card: this step carries -needs-card and waits for a card to itself.

items.title: The README shows what LiveEdit does: a source clip and its edit side by side at the editor's own size, with the instruction, as the other models show theirs

steps.title: The README's LiveEdit sample is a source clip and its edit at 832 x 480 side by side, the instruction stated, its time its own run's
steps.rationale: The owner's review of 2026-11-24 (fourth), checked against the README and the code: valid. The README's LiveEdit line links a 32 x 16 clip of 21 frames, states no instruction, shows no source clip, and says 9.5 s where the scorecard table says 10.2 s (the line's own run, not the scorecard's). The editor was trained at 832 x 480 (internal/latentvideo/edit_profiles.json source_width and source_height), and EditSourceSize (edit_form.go:103) says that at a quarter of that size it changes texture, not what the instruction asks; readme-media redid SenseNova, Un-0 and Wan and left LiveEdit. The change: a source clip at 832 x 480 (one of the VidGen clips the edit suite reads) edited by an instruction through go run ./cmd/recipe run -fresh, the source and the edit drawn side by side in one GIF, its caption naming the instruction, the seed, the frames and steps and the run's own time and memory, as the other models' samples are; the earlier clip and its file go. Check: the earlier clip is no longer linked, and the README's tests (repoanalysis, commanddoc) pass, among them TestReadmeNamesEveryModelAndItsSamples.

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
